---
title: "Constituency counts with Arrow"
output: html_notebook
---

How much does the share of cards marked deleted vary across constituencies?
One row is a physical card. Keep deleted cards in the denominator for this question.

```{r setup}
library(arrow)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

root <- path.expand("~/Documents/work/data_work/bangalore/voters/final_roll_2026")
data_dir <- file.path(root, "data")

open_dataset(data_dir) ->
  roll
```

```{r constituency-counts}
roll %>%
  summarise(
    cards = n(),
    deleted = sum(is_deleted, na.rm = TRUE),
    unread = sum(is.na(is_deleted)),
    .by = c(ac, constituency_name)
  ) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(
    retained = cards - deleted - unread,
    deleted_share = deleted / (cards - unread)
  ) ->
  constituency_counts
```

```{r totals}
constituency_counts %>%
  summarise(
    cards = sum(cards),
    retained = sum(retained),
    deleted = sum(deleted),
    unread = sum(unread)
  )
```

There are 65,883 deleted cards alongside 5,908,157 retained cards.
No unread deletion flags in this snapshot.

```{r deletion-plot}
constituency_counts %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = deleted_share,
    y = reorder(constituency_name, deleted_share)
  )) +
  geom_point(
    colour = "#0072B2",
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Bommanahalli has the highest share of cards marked deleted",
    subtitle = "28 Bangalore constituencies, November 2026 snapshot",
    x = "Deleted / all cards with known deletion status",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Source: final-roll card OCR. Includes accepted count exceptions."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

Bommanahalli is at 2.6%, against 0.2% in Pulakeshinagar.
These are deletion marks in the final snapshot; they cannot measure how many people were removed since an earlier roll.

What if I only want Jayanagar? Filter the dataset by constituency.

```{r one-constituency}
roll %>%
  filter(
    ac == 173,
    is_deleted == FALSE
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    retained = n(),
    female = sum(gender == "Female", na.rm = TRUE),
    unread_gender = sum(is.na(gender) | gender == "")
  ) %>%
  collect()
```
